interest: Shows wartime Japan subordinating zaibatsu-dominated markets through stock-exchange consolidation, and U.S. radio-intercept tracking of Tokyo stocks falling with Solomons losses.
overview: This file contains a January 20, 1943 memorandum prepared by F. S. Williams of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs in the U.S. Department of State, together with an attached radio broadcast intercept transcript of an address by Japanese Vice-Minister of Finance Tsuneji Taniguchi. The documents detail and analyze the Japanese Government's wartime legislative plan to reorganize its financial structure by dissolving existing private stock exchanges—most notably the Tokyo and Osaka stock exchanges and nine regional bourses—and replacing them by September 30, 1943, with the Japan Negotiable Securities Exchange, a unified government-controlled agency. The records examine the Imperial Japanese Government's objectives to curb market speculation, break the financial stranglehold of major zaibatsu cliques like Mitsui and Mitsubishi, rigidly control corporate capital issuance, and mobilize investment for heavy industries and the Greater East Asia Co-prosperity Sphere, while noting that Japanese equity markets plummeted following the announcement and recent military reversals in the Solomon Islands.

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum analyzing the Japanese Government's plan to dissolve private stock exchanges and establish a state-controlled securities exchange during wartime.
subfiles.summary: Williams reports Japan's bill dissolving the Tokyo and Osaka exchanges into a state-run Japan Negotiable Securities Exchange by September 1943, aimed at curbing zaibatsu dominance and speculation; stock prices fell sharply after Solomons naval losses and the reorganization announcement.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by F. S. Williams on Reform of Japanese Stock Exchanges
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A translated Japanese radio broadcast by Vice-Minister of Finance Taniguchi outlining the government's rationale and statutory provisions for nationalizing and reorganizing the stock exchanges.
subfiles.summary: In a domestic and imperial radio address, Vice-Minister of Finance Taniguchi explains the wartime necessity of restructuring Japan's stock exchanges to harmonize national production and secure people's savings. He asserts that private speculative trading and price volatility disrupt the wartime economy, requiring the unification of regional exchanges under government-appointed officials. The reform restricts market participants to qualified juridical entities and empowers the new organ to stabilize share values and facilitate capital issuance for national objectives. Taniguchi emphasizes that war-essential heavy industries and shipyards will be protected under the new system and appeals to exchange affiliates for full cooperation.
subfiles.title: Radio Address by Vice-Minister Taniguchi on the Reform of the Stock Exchange
